description:
Remove provider-specific policy from Accounts.People and shared identity orchestration through a canonical discovery/profile contract. User explicitly requested this epic after source investigation; Implementation was authorized and resumed by the user in the current checkout. Provider-neutral changes are implemented across both repositories; validation repairs are in progress.

Evidence: lib/zaq/accounts/people.ex consistent_discovered_owner/2 special-cases WhatsApp phone conflicts; profile_name/2 and profile_phone/2 inspect stored placeholders/JID suffixes. lib/zaq/people/identity_resolver.ex resolve_author/3 bypasses complete-profile optimization for WhatsApp. lib/zaq/people/resolver.ex owns WhatsApp push-name cleanup. Sibling Adapter.get_user/2 already returns UserInfo.metadata.phone and AmarulaClient.user_phone/2 owns connection-scoped LID mapping; Message.incoming_attrs/1 still passes raw pushname.

Acceptance: Accounts.People and shared identity orchestration contain no WhatsApp branches, JID suffix parsing, provider-specific placeholders, or equivalent disguised flags. Generic contracts distinguish identity evidence, profile enrichment, and replacement eligibility. Provider protocol interpretation stays in adapters/integration boundaries. People owns transactional identity/profile persistence and protects user edits. This integration has not shipped to production. Historical data repair, migration and legacy compatibility are out of scope; adapters never inspect Person rows. Preserve ordinary delayed enrichment and user edits for records created under the new contract. Preserve connector isolation, conflict rollback, delayed enrichment, concurrent discovery, and all existing non-WhatsApp semantics. No automatic merge based on display name or an enrichment phone. No new agent tool exposure.

Action reuse assessment: planning adds no executable operation. Implementation extends existing People.find_or_create_from_channel/2, PersonIdentities, Channels :fetch_profile, JidoChatBridge.fetch_profile/2 and adapter get_user/2; children record operation-specific decisions. Discovery checked domain APIs plus channels Actions, account tools and workflow steps; pairing Actions and workflow map/edge execution do not implement person discovery. Do not invent a parallel discovery Action.

Delivery: coordinated ZAQ and sibling package changes; complete regression validation before delivery; no legacy repair or compatibility rollout is required. Review any shared Jido schema extension before implementation; do not assume it is needed. Preserve existing worktree edits. Existing identity-actor-contract issues zaq-u3g/zaq-r35 are adjacent actor dispatch work, not duplicates.

Policies: read AGENTS.md, docs/agent-tools.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md and applicable module/service guidance before implementation. For sibling changes read ../jido_chat_whatsapp/AGENTS.md. Follow the authoritative validation lifecycle; preserve existing assertions. No commits, pushes or merges are authorized by this plan.
Mocking plan: keep internal modules and database boundaries real; isolate external transport at its existing contract, with connection-scoped offline fixtures. Avoid global configuration mutation.
E2E: no new UI or user journey; unit, property and thin integration tests provide the required coverage. Reassess if scope changes.


Dependency sequence (linear DAG; only contract definition is initially ready):
```mermaid
graph LR
  zaq_10n_1 --> zaq_10n_2
  zaq_10n_2 --> zaq_10n_3
  zaq_10n_3 --> zaq_10n_4
  zaq_10n_4 --> zaq_10n_6
  zaq_10n_6 --> zaq_10n_7
```

Steps:
- zaq-10n.1: Define the canonical identity and profile evidence contract
- zaq-10n.2: Normalize WhatsApp profile names at the adapter boundary
- zaq-10n.3: Translate adapter profiles into generic discovery and refresh evidence
- zaq-10n.4: Apply provider-neutral discovery and profile persistence in People
- zaq-10n.6: Validate provider-neutral discovery across all consumers
- zaq-10n.7: Complete review, coverage handoff and final validation
Implementation constraint confirmed with user: add no new ZAQ modules. Extend existing module responsibilities and existing canonical maps/callbacks. Do not introduce a discovery policy module, profile evidence module, wrapper Action, or provider-specific helper under People. Keep the contract minimal and document it in existing owners. If implementation evidence makes this constraint impossible, explain the concrete conflict before changing the agreed scope.

Required repository scope: implementation spans TWO repositories. The implementing agent must modify ../jido_chat_whatsapp (sibling of ZAQ; current absolute location /Users/jad/Desktop/Jad/workspace/zaq/forks/jat10/jido_chat_whatsapp) as well as ZAQ. Adapter changes are required work under zaq-10n.2, not a suggestion or a host-only workaround. Read each repository's AGENTS.md, inspect its Git state, and preserve existing edits. Track and report diffs and validation for both repositories. No commits or pushes are authorized.
title: [zaq-10n] Make People discovery and profile enrichment provider-neutral
